subclassFeature.name: The Party Lord
entries: Be it a literal god of revelry, an archmage holding more wealth than they know what to do with, or a lich who grew bored after conquering their realm; your patron is an all-powerful entity with a penchant for partying it down.

Using their amassed resources, they've transformed their dominion into a never-ending gathering of unrivaled scale, where beings from all corners of the multiverse come to celebrate and have a good time.
By making a pact with this vigorous lord of the night, you may partake from their dazzling magic, and gain exclusive invites to their domain! Maybe even access to the VIP areas...
So what are you waiting for? Let the festivities commence!

subclassFeature.name: Expanded Spell List
entries: The Party Lord lets you choose from an expanded, jazzy new list of options when you learn a warlock spell. The following spells are added to the warlock spell list for you.

entries.caption: Party Lord Expanded Spells
rows: 1st
{@spell Color Spray|PHB}, {@spell Tasha's Hideous Laughter|PHB}
2nd
{@spell Jim's Glowing Coin|AI}, {@spell Vortex Warp|SCC}
3rd
{@spell Fast Friends|AI}, {@spell Create Food and Water|PHB}
4th
{@spell Conjure Woodland Beings|PHB}, {@spell Aura of Life|PHB}
5th
{@spell Animate Objects|PHB}, {@spell Seeming|PHB}

subclassFeature.name: Funky Magical Phenomena
entries: At 1st level, your contract makes you the conduit for a very different kind of cosmic force.

Whenever you are subjected to an ability or spell that allows you to make a Dexterity or Wisdom saving throw to reduce or negate its effects, you can change it to a Charisma saving throw instead. You may use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and regain any expended uses when you finish a long rest.

Additionally, whenever you succeed on a Charisma check or saving throw, the DM must choose one cantrip from any spell list. For the next hour, you may cast that cantrip at will. You can only gain access to one cantrip at a time in this way.

subclassFeature.name: Legendary Invitation
entries: Your patron has used every bit of magic at their disposal to set up the most lavish and extravagant party of all time; and your name is on the guest list.

At 3rd level, you can perform a 1 minute ritual to summon a special invitation letter in your empty hand. It works similarly to a spell scroll, but doesn't require prior knowledge of the imbued magic or expending of any spell slots; burning away once it is used.

The letter can be used as an action on your turn, casting the {@spell Plane Shift|PHB} spell exclusively to teleport you and willing allies to your patron's realm. When casting it in this way, you can teleport a maximum number of creatures (including you) equal to your Charisma modifier + your proficiency bonus.

Once there, each creature must roll on the {@subclassFeature Party Shenanigans|Warlock|PHB|Party Lord|PartyLord|1} table to determine what happens to them during the event. You can spend up to a total of 1 hour on the party, after which all creatures who entered the venue through your letter are teleported back to where they were before. After you've used the invite, you must wait {@dice 1d6 + 1} days before you can summon a new one.

However, you may entice your patron's interest by performing great feats of artistic skill, or equally epic social blunders. Whenever you make a Charisma ability check or saving throw and roll a 1 or 20 on the {@dice d20}, you can subtract 1 day from the number of days remaining before you can summon an invite again.

If you feel that the teleporting nature of {@i Legendary Invitation} makes it too powerful by design, but would still like to make use of its flavour without balancing issues, you can add the following snippet to the feature's description:
{@b "This 3rd-level feature replaces the Pact Boon feature. You gain no benefit from the replaced feature and don't qualify for anything in the game that requires it."}

subclassFeature.name: Crash the Venue
entries: With such an eclectic mix of attendees, it's guaranteed that this party will be out of this world. At least your enemies will surely feel that way.

At 6th level, you can take unwilling hostile creatures along with you when casting the {@spell Plane Shift|PHB} spell through an invitation letter. Your targets must be within 15 feet of you in order for this to work. After arriving on your patron's realm, they must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, they are treated as being under the effects of the {@spell Confusion|PHB} spell, lasting for up to 1 hour. On a successful one, they must roll on the {@subclassFeature Party Shenanigans|Warlock|PHB|Party Lord|PartyLord|1} table as normal.
A creature is immune to your teleportation if it has legendary or lair actions, or the DM decides that the creature is too important for this to work.

subclassFeature.name: Revelry Unbound
entries: At 10th level, no appointment or woe can derail the festivities, for any time spent on the party is always a good time.

You and your fellow guests can now stay in your patron's realm for up to 8 hours. Whenever you do so, you can expend a warlock spell slot to make the time spent on the party count as a long rest for you and your companions.
Additionally, when bringing enemies along in the letter teleportation, you may now target foes within 20 feet of you.

subclassFeature.name: Plane that Never Sleeps
entries: At 14th level, you are able to truly experience what this party has to offer.

You and your companions are now VIP guests, being able to stay in your patron's realm for up to 24 hours at a time. Whenever you do so, you must wait an additional 7 days before you can summon an invite again.

Additionally, when rolling on the {@subclassFeature Party Shenanigans|Warlock|PHB|Party Lord|PartyLord|1} table (for any section except the 24-hour one), you may choose to roll an additional time and take either result. This does not apply for any creature other than yourself.
Lastly, when bringing enemies along in the letter teleportation, you may now target foes within 30 feet of you.

subclassFeature.name: Party Shenanigans
entries: A character must roll on this table to determine their experiences in the Party Lord's domain. Use each respective section for the total amount of time spent by characters on the realm, ranging from 1 minute, 10 minutes, 1 hour, 8 hours, or 24 hours. If the total time spent amounts to a different mensuration, round it down to the next lower section. {@b Example:} If the characters spent 3 hours at the party, round it down to the 1-hour section.
Alternatively, you may have them go through multiple outings of the next lower section instead. That usage of the mechanic is left to the DM's discretion.

If two or more player characters wish to stick together throughout their stay on the party, they may choose to make a single roll on this table to determine their shared outcome. If so, each individual character gains the specified effects from the resulting development.

When using the Party Shenanigans table, feel free to remove or add any number of your own options to it, as well as mix them around in their order. The objective is to maximize the amount of fun gained when roleplaying this archetype, so the only real limit here is your imagination (and the DM's patience for your shenanigans).

entries.caption: Party Shenanigans Table - 1 Minute
rows: You quickly grab what you can from the food servings. Gain {@dice 1d4} special treats, which last for 8 hours. A creature can use a bonus action to eat one of those treats, gaining {@dice 1d4 + 4} temporary hit points.

You try to bust a move on the dance floor, but end up slipping on a magical banana. Take {@damage 1d8} psychic damage, and gain a {@i Banana Peel}. It can be destroyed by a creature as a bonus action, granting them 2 sorcery points. These points are added to any sorcery points they have from another source, but can be used only on Metamagic.

A drunken dancer hurriedly approaches, and then promptly pukes all of their lunch over you. Take {@damage 1d6} acid damage and {@damage 1d6} psychic damage. Roll a {@dice d20}. If the number rolled is a 3 or lower, you become infected with the Sewer Plague.

You bump into the most gorgeous creature you've ever seen in your life, only for it to then escape your sight among the crowd. Gain a penalty of -2 to any Charisma ability checks or saving throws you make in the next 8 hours. {@b Special:} If you get this outcome again in less than 30 days, you can roll a {@dice d6}. If the number rolled is a 5 or 6, you meet with the original creature you stumbled upon. Gain a bonus of +4 to any Charisma ability checks or saving throws you make in the next 8 hours.

A couple of newlywed beholders ask you to take their painting. Make a Dexterity ({@skill Sleight of Hand}) or a Charisma ({@skill Performance}) check. On a result of 15 or higher, they greatly enjoy your depiction. Gain a tip of 50 gold. {@b Special:} On a result of 25 or higher, they perceive your work as a magnum opus, wanting to buy it from you instead. Make a Charisma ({@skill Persuasion}) check. On a result of 15 or lower, you sell the painting cheap for 300 gold. On a result of 16 or higher, you manage to bargain your way into a better deal, selling your work for 1000 gold.

A halfling bard with pink clothes tries to flirt his way into your life, but then accidentally turns himself into a pickle. Funniest thing you've ever seen. For the next {@dice 1d4} hours, you are treated as being under the effects of the {@spell Tasha's Hideous Laughter|PHB} spell.

You are suddenly recruited as the substitute priest for a wedding taking place in the ballroom. The universe decides that you are very good at it. For the next week, you gain access to the {@spell Ceremony|XGE} spell. It is considered a spell from your class list, and you always have it prepared; but it doesn't count against the number of spells you prepare each day. Once per long rest, you may cast it without expending a spell slot. {@b Special:} Whenever you get this outcome a total of 3 times, roll a {@dice d6}. If the number rolled is a 5 or 6, your priestdom is officially recognized by reality. You may cast the {@spell Ceremony|XGE} spell at will, without expending a spell slot.

A hurried autognome appears before you, seemingly trying to relay something urgent. Roll a {@dice d4}. On a 1 or 2, you are unable to understand any of it, prompting them to forcefully implant a chip into your head. Take {@damage 1d6} piercing damage. For the next 8 hours, you are treated as being under the effects of the {@spell Comprehend Languages|PHB} spell. On a 3 or 4, you discover that they wanted to tell you a new joke they just made up. It is a pun about locks. Take {@damage 1d6} psychic damage. For the next 8 hours, you have advantage on saving throws to resist being {@condition Charmed} or {@condition Frightened}.

entries.caption: Party Shenanigans Table - 10 Minutes
rows: You take your time to taste what the platters have to offer. Regain a number of hit points equal to {@dice 2d4} + your proficiency bonus. If you currently have no hit points to be recovered, gain a number of temporary hit points equal to four times your character level instead.

You engage in merrymaking with a friendly group of astral space hamsters, spending their interdimensional vacation in this party. Their bright energy permeates over to you, healing a bit of your soul in the process. Regain all of your expended spell slots. If you have no spell slots to be regained, then for the next 24 hours you may cast one spell of 5th level of lower once without expending a spell slot. If you don't possess a spellcasting ability, then for the next 24 hours you gain access to one use of the Action Surge feature from the Fighter class.
An interplanar trader offers you a small white pill, said to unlock the secrets of time-saving. Lose 50 gold. The pill can be consumed as a bonus action, granting you the effects of a short rest.

You get swept up in a makeshift slapping contest to determine the greatest gentlefolk of all. Make a Constitution saving throw ({@dc 14}). You take {@damage 3d4} psychic damage and {@damage 1d6} bludgeoning damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. Make a Strength ({@skill Athletics}), Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics}) or Charisma ({@skill Performance}) check. On a result of 18 or higher, you emerge victorious as the greatest slapper of this era. Your unarmed strikes can now be made in the form of slaps, dealing additional psychic damage equal to your proficiency bonus.

You engage in a lengthy discussion with a grey-haired human artificer, arguing about which beverage has the best flavor. After proving your taste buds to be superior, he whips out a strange firearm and warps you through a green portal. You arrive at a random location within a plane of the DM's choosing. If you are still in that plane after 24 hours, the human appears before you through a similar portal, and teleports you back to your original plane.

You are confused for an important political figure of a different plane's monarchy, leading a disguised royal agent to make an attempt at your life. Roll a {@dice d20}. On a 10 or higher, you manage to avoid their wrath by a hair's breadth, getting scarred from the experience. Gain {@dice 1d4} levels of {@condition Exhaustion}. On a 9 or lower, the agent manages to put a curse on you before getting suddenly consumed by a drunken owlbear sailor. For the next 24 hours, you cannot regain hit points in any way, or acquire any temporary hit points.

entries.caption: Party Shenanigans Table - 1 Hour
rows: You gorge yourself in the different pastries presented before you. Regain {@dice 2d6 + 2} hit points and gain {@dice 1d6} special treats, which last for 8 hours. A creature can use a bonus action to eat one of those treats, gaining {@dice 1d4 + 4} temporary hit points. For the next 12 hours, your speed is halved.

You bust a move on the dance floor, grooving to your heart's delight. Regain a number of hit points equal to {@dice 2d8} + your Charisma modifier. Make a Charisma ({@skill Performance}) check. On a result of 18 or higher, you are treated as being under the effects of the {@spell Kinetic Jaunt|SCC} spell for the next {@dice 1d8} hours.

You engage in a lyrical battle against a blue-haired gnome of funky beats. Make a Charisma ({@skill Performance}) and a Charisma ({@skill Intimidation}) check. On a result of 15 or higher for one of the two checks, the battle ends in a draw. Gain 1 level of {@condition Exhaustion}, which can be removed on a short rest. On a result of 15 or higher for both checks, you barely emerge victorious in the contest of syllables. Gain proficiency in the {@skill Performance} skill. If you are already proficient in this skill, you gain advantage on Charisma checks for the next {@dice 1d8} hours. On a result of 14 or lower for both checks, the funky gnome wipes the floor with your tumbling butt. You become {@condition Stunned} for the next {@dice 1d4} hours.

An elf clad in black leather and sporting a wild hairstyle challenges you to an epic duel in their children's card game. Make an Intelligence or Wisdom check. You can add your proficiency bonus to this roll if you have proficiency with the Playing Card Set. On a result of 18 or higher, you miraculously win the match, impressing the eccentric elf and attaining his favor. Gain a single {@i Monster Card}, choosing from Fey, Demon, Shadow, Undead or Warrior. Each of those cards can be used to cast the {@spell Summon Fey|TCE}, {@spell Summon Lesser Demons|XGE}, {@spell Summon Shadowspawn|TCE}, {@spell Summon Undead|TCE}, or Summon Warrior Spirit (UA) spells, respectively. You must use your own spell slots in order to cast one of these spells through their respective card. When you do so, they don't require material components.

A strange hooded sorcerer throws a mysterious dust in your face. You fall into a magical slumber and take a {@b very good} nap. Gain the effects of a long rest. If magic can't put you to sleep, you enter a sneezing fit instead. Gain a penalty of -2 to any ability checks or saving throws you make in the next {@dice 1d4} hours.

You eat the wrong cockatrice sandwich, and end up spending a not-so-great time on the privy chamber. You take {@damage 2d6} psychic damage, and become {@condition Poisoned} for the next {@dice 2d4} hours.

You meet a talking magical unicorn who starts lecturing you on the power of friendship. Make a Constitution saving throw, a Wisdom ({@skill Survival}) check or an Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) check. On a result of 15 or higher, you manage to survive the encounter with your mind intact. Gain 1 level of {@condition Exhaustion}. For the next 24 hours, you have a +1 bonus to your Intelligence modifier. If the result is 14 or lower, your eyes are opened to the unrivaled magic one can find within their bonds. For the next {@dice 1d4} weeks, you may cast the {@spell Friends|PHB} cantrip at will without material components, but have disadvantage on saving throws to resist being {@condition Charmed}.

You play a few matches of life-sized chess with the local party-goers. Make four Intelligence or Wisdom ({@skill Insight}) checks. You can add your proficiency bonus to the rolls if you have proficiency with the Dragonchess Set. On a result of 15 or higher for a check, your wits prove superior to your opponent's for that match. If you win at least three of your matches, a member of the audience decides to reward you for the good games. Gain one common wondrous item of the DM's choosing. If you win all four of your matches, gain proficiency with the Dragonchess set if you didn't already have it. If you lose three or more of your matches, the taste of utter defeat crushes your self-confidence. For the next {@dice 1d4} days, you have disadvantage on any Intelligence or Charisma checks and saving throws you make.

entries.caption: Party Shenanigans Table - 8 Hours
rows: You take part in a lavish banquet of glorious proportions. You are treated as being under the effects of the {@spell Heroes' Feast|PHB} spell. For the next 24 hours, your speed is halved.

You perform a series of group dances with choreographic perfection, even though you've never met any of your partners before. Gain 2 levels of {@condition Exhaustion}. For the next 24 hours, you are treated as being under the effects of the {@spell Kinetic Jaunt|SCC} spell.

You spend a relaxing time on the hot tub with a bunch of fellow partygoers. The magical healing waters wash your worries away, leaving your body perhaps a little {@i too relaxed}. You are treated as being under the effects of the {@spell Heal|PHB} spell. For the next 24 hours, you have resistance to acid, cold, fire, and poison damage, but gain a penalty of -4 to your Strength modifier and disadvantage on any Strength checks or Constitution saving throws you make.

You participate on a cart race against a gnome artificer of red and blue clothes, along with many other curious competitors. Make a Dexterity check. You can add your proficiency bonus to this roll if you have proficiency with land vehicles. On a result of 16 or higher, you place in the top 5. Gain a +2 bonus to ability checks and saving throws for the next {@dice 2d6} hours. On a result of 20 or higher, you place 1st in the race. Gain proficiency with land vehicles if you didn't already have it, and a +4 bonus to ability checks and saving throws for the next {@dice 2d8} hours.

You are taken by a hefty aristocrat through a {@i 'Socializing 101'} emergency crash course. For the next 24 hours, you learn the {@spell Charm Monster|XGE} spell and may cast the {@spell Friends|PHB} cantrip at will. {@b Special:} If you get this outcome a total of 3 times, you gain proficiency in the {@skill Persuasion} skill. If you are already proficient in this skill, you gain expertise with it instead (does not stack with similar features).

You are enraptured by a changeling mime, whose loony antics leave you dumbfounded out of your mind. Make a Wisdom check. On a result of 15 or higher, you are treated as being under the effects of the {@spell Confusion|PHB} spell for the next {@dice 1d4} hours. On a result of 14 or lower, you are treated as being under the effects of the {@spell Mental Prison|XGE} spell for the next {@dice 2d6} hours.

entries.caption: Party Shenanigans Table - 24 Hours
rows: You are met by a pompous elf wearing a white sleeveless coat with shoulder pads and a raised collar. He announces himself to be the greatest gamer of all, and challenges you for the title of King of Cards. Make an Intelligence, Wisdom or Charisma check. You can add your proficiency bonus to this roll if you have proficiency with the Playing Card Set. On a result of 22 or higher, you emerge victorious against the egocentric elf, taking his greatest treasure as your reward. You gain the {@i Azure-Eyes Silver Dragon} card. This item can be used to cast the {@spell Summon Draconic Spirit|FTD} spell without material components. You must use your own spell slots in order to cast it through the card in this way. When you do so, the summoned spirit benefits from all three family types. {@b Special:} This outcome can only happen if you've gained a {@i Monster Card} item from a previous roll of the Party Shenanigans table. If this prerequisite is not met, you go through four outings of the fourth outcome from the 1-hour section instead.

After chatting the hours away in the counter, you are offered an extravagant cocktail from the local warforged bartender, which unbeknownst to you is spiked with wild magic. Roll a {@dice d6}. Choose a spell of a level equal to the number rolled, from any spell list. It is now considered a spell from your class list, and you always have it prepared; but it doesn't count against the number of spells you prepare each day. If you don't possess a spellcasting ability, then you may cast it by expending a number of hit dice equal to the spell's level. When casting the spell in this way, it doesn't require material components.

You end up being pulled along into a secret heist of one of the many vaults in this seemingly infinite venue. Roll a {@dice d20}. On a 9 or lower, gain one magic item with a rarity of Uncommon or lower. On a 10 or higher, gain one magic item with a rarity of Rare or lower. On a 16 or higher, gain one magic item with a rarity of Very Rare or lower. Which item is given to your character, as well as what rarity that variant of it possesses, can either be determined by the DM or left entirely to your choice (with their approval). The effects of that decision on the campaign are left to the DM's discretion. {@b Special:} Whenever this outcome is experienced by player characters a total of 3 times, the DM must roll a {@dice d6}. On a 4 or lower, one of the party's chief stewards takes knowledge of this repeated robbery, seeking monetary transference in return. You and all of your party members lose every gold (or platinum) piece you are currently in possession of.

You meet and spend the day with an elder dragon archpriest, who offers you the redefining of your own soul. You may change your current subclass if you wish so. This can only be done once per character. The effects of this decision on the campaign are left to the DM's discretion.

You are reunited with a being you once met in this never-ending party. Roll a {@dice d6}. On a 3 or lower, the creature is hostile towards you. They will attempt to engage in combat with you and your companions, and may follow your trail even after you leave your patron's realm (if they are capable of doing so). The creature's stats and abilities, as well as how their battle with you affects your companions' time in the party, are left to the DM's discretion. If the number rolled is a 4 or higher, you and the creature develop a lasting friendship. They will attempt to accompany you after leaving your patron's realm, doing their best to help on your group's quests. At the DM's discretion, they can become a reoccurring or permanent ally NPC.

After experiencing the joys of Happy Hour, you decide to take part in a grand drinking contest; only to find out you can't hold your liquor nearly as well as you thought. For the next {@dice 2d4} days, you have disadvantage on any attack rolls, ability checks or saving throws you make.

While dilly-dallying your way through the multifarious chambers of this realm, you end up taking a peek into a room you shouldn't have. The DM must choose one specific type of creature, object, scenery and event. For the next year, you become {@condition Frightened} whenever you catch sight of the chosen subjects. The condition lasts for as long as one of the subjects remains in your sight. {@b Example:} The chosen subjects can be a lute, a bathroom, and a fey creature. Your character will instantly become {@condition Frightened} when seeing any of those things.

You gain the one-in-a-million chance to meet the very entity who makes all of this possible: {@b your patron, the Party Lord}. You can ask up to five questions, as per the {@spell Commune|PHB} spell. The answers are left to the DM's discretion. Make a Charisma check. You may cast any number of spells or apply any number of effects on yourself before making the roll. On a result of 25 or higher, your patron's time with you proves entertaining enough for them to dole out a gift of appreciation. You gain one use of the {@spell Wish|PHB} spell. This can only be done once per year. {@b Special:} This outcome can only happen if your character is the holder of this subclass. If this prerequisite is not met, you go through two different outcomes from the 8-hour section instead. You must make a separate roll to determine each one.

optionalfeature.name: Portal Shake
entries: You may cast {@spell Vortex Warp|SCC} once as a 2nd-level spell, without expending a spell slot. When casting it in this way, you target a number of creatures (including yourself) equal to your Charisma modifier + your proficiency bonus.
You can use this feature a number of times per long rest equal to half your proficiency bonus (rounded up).

optionalfeature.name: Inebriated Casting
entries: Whenever you become intoxicated by alcohol, you can roll on the {@table Wild Magic Surge|PHB} table to create a magical effect. If that effect is a spell, it can't be affected by Metamagic, and if it normally requires concentration, it doesn't require concentration in this case; lasting for its full duration.
Once you've used this feature, you cannot do so again until you finish a long rest and get intoxicated again.

optionalfeature.name: Magical Osmosis
entries: Your constant interaction with beings of all kinds, and from many different realms, has exposed you to distinct types of magic which you've unconsciously absorbed. You learn two cantrips of your choice from the following options: {@spell Prestidigitation|PHB}, {@spell Minor Illusion|PHB}, {@spell Thaumaturgy|PHB}, {@spell Druidcraft|PHB}, {@spell Dancing Lights|PHB}. They count as warlock spells for you, even if they are not on the warlock spell list.

optionalfeature.name: Theme Song
entries: You learn the Unearthly Chorus spell (UA), but may only cast it with a slot of 2nd level or higher. It counts as a warlock spell for you, but doesn't count against the number of spells you know.

optionalfeature.name: Boozy Desserts
entries: You may cast {@spell Goodberry|PHB} once without expending a spell slot. When casting it in this way, you can summon 1 extra treat for each ally that is within 15 feet of you.

Any creature that eats one of your treats regains an additional number of hit points equal to your Charisma modifier, but must succeed on a Constitution saving throw ({@dc 12}) or become {@condition Poisoned} for 1 hour. The DC increases by +2 for each new treat they consume before their next long rest, and the condition's duration increases by 1 hour for each new failed save they make before it ends.
Once you've used this feature, you cannot do so again until you finish a long rest.

optionalfeature.name: Cross-Plane Networking
entries: Whenever you find yourself at a social gathering of any kind, be it the old village tavern or a meeting of the evil cult's leaders, you gain access to the {@spell Tongues|PHB} spell; temporarily adding it to your list of spells known. It remains on the list for the remainder of the event, and you may cast it without material components.

optionalfeature.name: Life of the Party
entries: You may channel the boundless energy of your patron's realm, permeating the space around you with frolicking delight. As an action on your turn, you create a 30-foot-radius area centered on you.

For the next hour, any intelligent creature that enters the area or starts its turn there must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, the creature starts to engage in celebratory revelry: drinking, singing, laughing, and dancing. Affected creatures are reluctant to leave the area until this effect ends, preferring to continue the festivities.

They forsake appointments, cease caring about their woes, and generally behave in a cordial (if not hedonistic) manner. This preoccupation with merrymaking occurs regardless of an affected creature's agenda or alignment. Assassins procrastinate, servants join in the celebration rather than working, and guards abandon their posts.

The effect ends on a creature when it is attacked, takes damage, or is forced to leave the area. A creature that makes a successful saving throw can enter or leave the area without danger of being enchanted. A creature that fails the saving throw and is forcibly removed from the area must repeat the saving throw if it returns to the area.
Once you've used this feature, you must wait {@dice 1d4} days before you can do so again.

optionalfeature.name: Disco Ball
entries: As an action on your turn, you can summon a mirrored sphere of glittering lights which mesmerizes all near it, compelling them to enter the groove. The sphere appears in an unoccupied space of your choice within 30 feet of you, lasting for 1 minute. All creatures within 20 feet of the sphere that can see or hear it must make a Charisma saving throw. On a failed save, they are treated as being under the effects of the {@spell Otto's Irresistible Dance|PHB} spell. Once you've used this feature, you cannot do so again until you finish a long rest.

optionalfeature.name: Zero Groovity Bash
entries: You may cast {@spell Reverse Gravity|PHB} once without expending a spell slot. You can't do so again until you finish a long rest.

optionalfeature.name: Rave Lights
entries: You may cast {@spell Prismatic Spray|PHB} once without expending a spell slot. You can't do so again until you finish a long rest.

optionalfeature.name: VIP Access
entries: As a VIP guest, you are granted entry to even more exclusive parts of your patron's domain. If you have an invitation letter on hand, you may cast {@spell Mordenkainen's Magnificent Mansion|PHB} once without expending a spell slot.

When casting it in this way, you don't choose the dwelling's appearance or furnishing, the servants have random non-transparent attires, and many other unknown creatures are also present within its space. All of those details are instead left to the DM's discretion. Once you've used this feature, you must wait one week before you can do so again.

table.name: Party Shenanigans Table - 1 Minute
rows: You quickly grab what you can from the food servings. Gain {@dice 1d4} special treats, which last for 8 hours. A creature can use a bonus action to eat one of those treats, gaining {@dice 1d4 + 4} temporary hit points.

You try to bust a move on the dance floor, but end up slipping on a magical banana. Take {@damage 1d8} psychic damage, and gain a {@i Banana Peel}. It can be destroyed by a creature as a bonus action, granting them 2 sorcery points. These points are added to any sorcery points they have from another source, but can be used only on Metamagic.

A drunken dancer hurriedly approaches, and then promptly pukes all of their lunch over you. Take {@damage 1d6} acid damage and {@damage 1d6} psychic damage. Roll a {@dice d20}. If the number rolled is a 3 or lower, you become infected with the Sewer Plague.

You bump into the most gorgeous creature you've ever seen in your life, only for it to then escape your sight among the crowd. Gain a penalty of -2 to any Charisma ability checks or saving throws you make in the next 8 hours. {@b Special:} If you get this outcome again in less than 30 days, you can roll a {@dice d6}. If the number rolled is a 5 or 6, you meet with the original creature you stumbled upon. Gain a bonus of +4 to any Charisma ability checks or saving throws you make in the next 8 hours.

A couple of newlywed beholders ask you to take their painting. Make a Dexterity ({@skill Sleight of Hand}) or a Charisma ({@skill Performance}) check. On a result of 15 or higher, they greatly enjoy your depiction. Gain a tip of 50 gold. {@b Special:} On a result of 25 or higher, they perceive your work as a magnum opus, wanting to buy it from you instead. Make a Charisma ({@skill Persuasion}) check. On a result of 15 or lower, you sell the painting cheap for 300 gold. On a result of 16 or higher, you manage to bargain your way into a better deal, selling your work for 1000 gold.

A halfling bard with pink clothes tries to flirt his way into your life, but then accidentally turns himself into a pickle. Funniest thing you've ever seen. For the next {@dice 1d4} hours, you are treated as being under the effects of the {@spell Tasha's Hideous Laughter|PHB} spell.

You are suddenly recruited as the substitute priest for a wedding taking place in the ballroom. The universe decides that you are very good at it. For the next week, you gain access to the {@spell Ceremony|XGE} spell. It is considered a spell from your class list, and you always have it prepared; but it doesn't count against the number of spells you prepare each day. Once per long rest, you may cast it without expending a spell slot. {@b Special:} Whenever you get this outcome a total of 3 times, roll a {@dice d6}. If the number rolled is a 5 or 6, your priestdom is officially recognized by reality. You may cast the {@spell Ceremony|XGE} spell at will, without expending a spell slot.

A hurried autognome appears before you, seemingly trying to relay something urgent. Roll a {@dice d4}. On a 1 or 2, you are unable to understand any of it, prompting them to forcefully implant a chip into your head. Take {@damage 1d6} piercing damage. For the next 8 hours, you are treated as being under the effects of the {@spell Comprehend Languages|PHB} spell. On a 3 or 4, you discover that they wanted to tell you a new joke they just made up. It is a pun about locks. Take {@damage 1d6} psychic damage. For the next 8 hours, you have advantage on saving throws to resist being {@condition Charmed} or {@condition Frightened}.

table.name: Party Shenanigans Table - 10 Minutes
rows: You take your time to taste what the platters have to offer. Regain a number of hit points equal to {@dice 2d4} + your proficiency bonus. If you currently have no hit points to be recovered, gain a number of temporary hit points equal to four times your character level instead.

You engage in merrymaking with a friendly group of astral space hamsters, spending their interdimensional vacation in this party. Their bright energy permeates over to you, healing a bit of your soul in the process. Regain all of your expended spell slots. If you have no spell slots to be regained, then for the next 24 hours you may cast one spell of 5th level of lower once without expending a spell slot. If you don't possess a spellcasting ability, then for the next 24 hours you gain access to one use of the Action Surge feature from the Fighter class.
An interplanar trader offers you a small white pill, said to unlock the secrets of time-saving. Lose 50 gold. The pill can be consumed as a bonus action, granting you the effects of a short rest.

You get swept up in a makeshift slapping contest to determine the greatest gentlefolk of all. Make a Constitution saving throw ({@dc 14}). You take {@damage 3d4} psychic damage and {@damage 1d6} bludgeoning damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. Make a Strength ({@skill Athletics}), Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics}) or Charisma ({@skill Performance}) check. On a result of 18 or higher, you emerge victorious as the greatest slapper of this era. Your unarmed strikes can now be made in the form of slaps, dealing additional psychic damage equal to your proficiency bonus.

You engage in a lengthy discussion with a grey-haired human artificer, arguing about which beverage has the best flavor. After proving your taste buds to be superior, he whips out a strange firearm and warps you through a green portal. You arrive at a random location within a plane of the DM's choosing. If you are still in that plane after 24 hours, the human appears before you through a similar portal, and teleports you back to your original plane.

You are confused for an important political figure of a different plane's monarchy, leading a disguised royal agent to make an attempt at your life. Roll a {@dice d20}. On a 10 or higher, you manage to avoid their wrath by a hair's breadth, getting scarred from the experience. Gain {@dice 1d4} levels of {@condition Exhaustion}. On a 9 or lower, the agent manages to put a curse on you before getting suddenly consumed by a drunken owlbear sailor. For the next 24 hours, you cannot regain hit points in any way, or acquire any temporary hit points.

table.name: Party Shenanigans Table - 1 Hour
rows: You gorge yourself in the different pastries presented before you. Regain {@dice 2d6 + 2} hit points and gain {@dice 1d6} special treats, which last for 8 hours. A creature can use a bonus action to eat one of those treats, gaining {@dice 1d4 + 4} temporary hit points. For the next 12 hours, your speed is halved.

You bust a move on the dance floor, grooving to your heart's delight. Regain a number of hit points equal to {@dice 2d8} + your Charisma modifier. Make a Charisma ({@skill Performance}) check. On a result of 18 or higher, you are treated as being under the effects of the {@spell Kinetic Jaunt|SCC} spell for the next {@dice 1d8} hours.

You engage in a lyrical battle against a blue-haired gnome of funky beats. Make a Charisma ({@skill Performance}) and a Charisma ({@skill Intimidation}) check. On a result of 15 or higher for one of the two checks, the battle ends in a draw. Gain 1 level of {@condition Exhaustion}, which can be removed on a short rest. On a result of 15 or higher for both checks, you barely emerge victorious in the contest of syllables. Gain proficiency in the {@skill Performance} skill. If you are already proficient in this skill, you gain advantage on Charisma checks for the next {@dice 1d8} hours. On a result of 14 or lower for both checks, the funky gnome wipes the floor with your tumbling butt. You become {@condition Stunned} for the next {@dice 1d4} hours.

An elf clad in black leather and sporting a wild hairstyle challenges you to an epic duel in their children's card game. Make an Intelligence or Wisdom check. You can add your proficiency bonus to this roll if you have proficiency with the Playing Card Set. On a result of 18 or higher, you miraculously win the match, impressing the eccentric elf and attaining his favor. Gain a single {@i Monster Card}, choosing from Fey, Demon, Shadow, Undead or Warrior. Each of those cards can be used to cast the {@spell Summon Fey|TCE}, {@spell Summon Lesser Demons|XGE}, {@spell Summon Shadowspawn|TCE}, {@spell Summon Undead|TCE}, or Summon Warrior Spirit (UA) spells, respectively. You must use your own spell slots in order to cast one of these spells through their respective card. When you do so, they don't require material components.

A strange hooded sorcerer throws a mysterious dust in your face. You fall into a magical slumber and take a {@b very good} nap. Gain the effects of a long rest. If magic can't put you to sleep, you enter a sneezing fit instead. Gain a penalty of -2 to any ability checks or saving throws you make in the next {@dice 1d4} hours.

You eat the wrong cockatrice sandwich, and end up spending a not-so-great time on the privy chamber. You take {@damage 2d6} psychic damage, and become {@condition Poisoned} for the next {@dice 2d4} hours.

You meet a talking magical unicorn who starts lecturing you on the power of friendship. Make a Constitution saving throw, a Wisdom ({@skill Survival}) check or an Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) check. On a result of 15 or higher, you manage to survive the encounter with your mind intact. Gain 1 level of {@condition Exhaustion}. For the next 24 hours, you have a +1 bonus to your Intelligence modifier. If the result is 14 or lower, your eyes are opened to the unrivaled magic one can find within their bonds. For the next {@dice 1d4} weeks, you may cast the {@spell Friends|PHB} cantrip at will without material components, but have disadvantage on saving throws to resist being {@condition Charmed}.

You play a few matches of life-sized chess with the local party-goers. Make four Intelligence or Wisdom ({@skill Insight}) checks. You can add your proficiency bonus to the rolls if you have proficiency with the Dragonchess Set. On a result of 15 or higher for a check, your wits prove superior to your opponent's for that match. If you win at least three of your matches, a member of the audience decides to reward you for the good games. Gain one common wondrous item of the DM's choosing. If you win all four of your matches, gain proficiency with the Dragonchess set if you didn't already have it. If you lose three or more of your matches, the taste of utter defeat crushes your self-confidence. For the next {@dice 1d4} days, you have disadvantage on any Intelligence or Charisma checks and saving throws you make.

table.name: Party Shenanigans Table - 8 Hours
rows: You take part in a lavish banquet of glorious proportions. You are treated as being under the effects of the {@spell Heroes' Feast|PHB} spell. For the next 24 hours, your speed is halved.

You perform a series of group dances with choreographic perfection, even though you've never met any of your partners before. Gain 2 levels of {@condition Exhaustion}. For the next 24 hours, you are treated as being under the effects of the {@spell Kinetic Jaunt|SCC} spell.

You spend a relaxing time on the hot tub with a bunch of fellow partygoers. The magical healing waters wash your worries away, leaving your body perhaps a little {@i too relaxed}. You are treated as being under the effects of the {@spell Heal|PHB} spell. For the next 24 hours, you have resistance to acid, cold, fire, and poison damage, but gain a penalty of -4 to your Strength modifier and disadvantage on any Strength checks or Constitution saving throws you make.

You participate on a cart race against a gnome artificer of red and blue clothes, along with many other curious competitors. Make a Dexterity check. You can add your proficiency bonus to this roll if you have proficiency with land vehicles. On a result of 16 or higher, you place in the top 5. Gain a +2 bonus to ability checks and saving throws for the next {@dice 2d6} hours. On a result of 20 or higher, you place 1st in the race. Gain proficiency with land vehicles if you didn't already have it, and a +4 bonus to ability checks and saving throws for the next {@dice 2d8} hours.

You are taken by a hefty aristocrat through a {@i 'Socializing 101'} emergency crash course. For the next 24 hours, you learn the {@spell Charm Monster|XGE} spell and may cast the {@spell Friends|PHB} cantrip at will. {@b Special:} If you get this outcome a total of 3 times, you gain proficiency in the {@skill Persuasion} skill. If you are already proficient in this skill, you gain expertise with it instead (does not stack with similar features).

You are enraptured by a changeling mime, whose loony antics leave you dumbfounded out of your mind. Make a Wisdom check. On a result of 15 or higher, you are treated as being under the effects of the {@spell Confusion|PHB} spell for the next {@dice 1d4} hours. On a result of 14 or lower, you are treated as being under the effects of the {@spell Mental Prison|XGE} spell for the next {@dice 2d6} hours.

table.name: Party Shenanigans Table - 24 Hours
rows: You are met by a pompous elf wearing a white sleeveless coat with shoulder pads and a raised collar. He announces himself to be the greatest gamer of all, and challenges you for the title of King of Cards. Make an Intelligence, Wisdom or Charisma check. You can add your proficiency bonus to this roll if you have proficiency with the Playing Card Set. On a result of 22 or higher, you emerge victorious against the egocentric elf, taking his greatest treasure as your reward. You gain the {@i Azure-Eyes Silver Dragon} card. This item can be used to cast the {@spell Summon Draconic Spirit|FTD} spell without material components. You must use your own spell slots in order to cast it through the card in this way. When you do so, the summoned spirit benefits from all three family types. {@b Special:} This outcome can only happen if you've gained a {@i Monster Card} item from a previous roll of the Party Shenanigans table. If this prerequisite is not met, you go through four outings of the fourth outcome from the 1-hour section instead.

After chatting the hours away in the counter, you are offered an extravagant cocktail from the local warforged bartender, which unbeknownst to you is spiked with wild magic. Roll a {@dice d6}. Choose a spell of a level equal to the number rolled, from any spell list. It is now considered a spell from your class list, and you always have it prepared; but it doesn't count against the number of spells you prepare each day. If you don't possess a spellcasting ability, then you may cast it by expending a number of hit dice equal to the spell's level. When casting the spell in this way, it doesn't require material components.

You end up being pulled along into a secret heist of one of the many vaults in this seemingly infinite venue. Roll a {@dice d20}. On a 9 or lower, gain one magic item with a rarity of Uncommon or lower. On a 10 or higher, gain one magic item with a rarity of Rare or lower. On a 16 or higher, gain one magic item with a rarity of Very Rare or lower. Which item is given to your character, as well as what rarity that variant of it possesses, can either be determined by the DM or left entirely to your choice (with their approval). The effects of that decision on the campaign are left to the DM's discretion. {@b Special:} Whenever this outcome is experienced by player characters a total of 3 times, the DM must roll a {@dice d6}. On a 4 or lower, one of the party's chief stewards takes knowledge of this repeated robbery, seeking monetary transference in return. You and all of your party members lose every gold (or platinum) piece you are currently in possession of.

You meet and spend the day with an elder dragon archpriest, who offers you the redefining of your own soul. You may change your current subclass if you wish so. This can only be done once per character. The effects of this decision on the campaign are left to the DM's discretion.

You are reunited with a being you once met in this never-ending party. Roll a {@dice d6}. On a 3 or lower, the creature is hostile towards you. They will attempt to engage in combat with you and your companions, and may follow your trail even after you leave your patron's realm (if they are capable of doing so). The creature's stats and abilities, as well as how their battle with you affects your companions' time in the party, are left to the DM's discretion. If the number rolled is a 4 or higher, you and the creature develop a lasting friendship. They will attempt to accompany you after leaving your patron's realm, doing their best to help on your group's quests. At the DM's discretion, they can become a reoccurring or permanent ally NPC.

After experiencing the joys of Happy Hour, you decide to take part in a grand drinking contest; only to find out you can't hold your liquor nearly as well as you thought. For the next {@dice 2d4} days, you have disadvantage on any attack rolls, ability checks or saving throws you make.

While dilly-dallying your way through the multifarious chambers of this realm, you end up taking a peek into a room you shouldn't have. The DM must choose one specific type of creature, object, scenery and event. For the next year, you become {@condition Frightened} whenever you catch sight of the chosen subjects. The condition lasts for as long as one of the subjects remains in your sight. {@b Example:} The chosen subjects can be a lute, a bathroom, and a fey creature. Your character will instantly become {@condition Frightened} when seeing any of those things.

You gain the one-in-a-million chance to meet the very entity who makes all of this possible: {@b your patron, the Party Lord}. You can ask up to five questions, as per the {@spell Commune|PHB} spell. The answers are left to the DM's discretion. Make a Charisma check. You may cast any number of spells or apply any number of effects on yourself before making the roll. On a result of 25 or higher, your patron's time with you proves entertaining enough for them to dole out a gift of appreciation. You gain one use of the {@spell Wish|PHB} spell. This can only be done once per year. {@b Special:} This outcome can only happen if your character is the holder of this subclass. If this prerequisite is not met, you go through two different outcomes from the 8-hour section instead. You must make a separate roll to determine each one.
